Author: Hiranmay Bhattacharyya Bench: Hiranmay Bhattacharyya 09.12.2024  Item No. 1  PG  Ct. No.7  W.P.A. 7400 of 2015  Sufera Bibi  Vs.
 State of West Bengal & Ors.
 Mr. Amit Kr. Pan  Ms. Tanusri Santra .........for the petitioner  Mr. Sirsanya Bandyopadhyay, Ld. Jr. Standing Counsel  .....for the State  Ms. Manika Roy  Ms. Ankita Chowdhury  Mr. Atanu Sur ................for the NHAI

1 . The petitioner claims that her father viz., Masum Saikh  (since deceased) was the owner of R.S. Plot Nos. 191  and 198 corresponding to L.R. Plot Nos. 227 and 234  respectively within Mouza-Joykrishnapur, J.L. No. 85  under Police Station-Samsherganj, District-  Murshidabad.

2. For the purpose of providing proper facilitation for  transportation namely, for realignment/modification of  National Highway 34 due to construction of Farakka  Barrage, an order under section 3(1) of the West Bengal  Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948 (for short  'Act II of 1948') was issued.

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that notice under section 4(1a) of Act  II of 1948 was neither served either upon the  2  predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner or upon the  petitioner nor published in the Official Gazette.

4. Mr. Pan, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner  submits that after the expiry of Act II of 1948, no step  was taken by the State for acquiring the property by  resorting to the provisions of section 9(3A) of the Land  Acquisition (West Bengal Amendment) Act, 1997.

Mr.
 Pan submits that though the land of the petitioner has  been utilised for the purpose for which the order under section 3(1) of Act II of 1948 was issued but no  compensation amount has been paid to the petitioner  till date.
5.

Mr. Bandyopadhyay, learned Junior Standing Counsel,
 in his usual fairness, submits that no notice under section 9(3A) of the West Bengal Land Acquisition  (Amendment) Act, 1997 was served.
He further submits  that no award in connection with the said plots of land  has been made.

6. Mr. Bandyopadhyay submits that the Government of  West Bengal Land and Land Reforms Department, Land  Policy Branch issued a Memorandum being No. 756-  LP/1A-03/14(Pt.-II) dated February 25, 2016, which is Sufera Bibi vs State Of West Bengal & Ors on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76329108/
2  popularly known as Direct Land Purchase Policy from  Land Owners by the Government.
7.

entities.text: Government of  West Bengal Land and Land Reforms Department
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Sufera Bibi vs State Of West Bengal & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Bandyopadhyay, upon instructions, submits that  the State Government is willing to purchase the land  3  directly from the petitioner in terms of the aforesaid  policy.

8. Mr. Pan, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner  submits that the petitioner cannot take a decision  merely on the basis of the submission advanced by the  learned Junior Standing Counsel for the State.
9. In reply, Mr. Bandyopadhyay prays for an  accommodation to file an affidavit in that regard on or  before the next date of hearing.
10. As prayed for by Mr. Bandyopadhyay, the Special  Land Acquisition Officer,

Murshidabad being the 3 rd  respondent will be at liberty to file an affidavit stating as to whether the State Government is ready and willing to purchase the land directly from the writ petitioner in terms of the said policy and the time-limit within which the entire process shall be concluded.

11. Let such affidavit be filed by the 3 rd respondent on or before December 20, 2024 upon giving an advance copy of the same to the learned advocate on record of the petitioner.
12. List this matter on December 23, 2024.
(HIRANMAY BHATTACHARYYA, J.)
